key_insight: The paper derives a reduced kinetic-to-fluid description for dilute gases with time-dependent helical symmetry, showing how geometry and deformation create anisotropic stresses and transport effects.
engineering_relevance: It provides a more physically faithful model for predicting flow, stress, and temperature in helical or cylindrical devices where axial deformation and heat transfer matter.
method: Derives a reduced Boltzmann equation that keeps radial variation while preserving the classical collision operator.
Uses formal hydrodynamic expansion to obtain Euler and Navier–Stokes–Fourier equations under helical symmetry.
Compares the reduced models against direct simulation Monte Carlo for uniform and radially varying flows.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that first-order fluid corrections capture leading stress anisotropy and improve radial temperature prediction in the tested cases.
watch_item: Accuracy degrades at larger Knudsen numbers, so the continuum closure may miss stronger rarefaction effects.
paper_title: Kinetic Reduction and Hydrodynamics under Time-Dependent Helical Symmetry
